Complete combinations + how to cook them

Bowls

Start with combinations built from regular ingredients. Every cooked protein includes its method; fruit, feta and pickles are clearly treated as toppings rather than mysterious bowl names.

01

Everyday rotation

Greens, Pacha and crucifers lead. Quinoa or wild rice is optional; spaghetti squash is only a swap when it happens to be around.

Cook fresh

Mango salmon

Base
Greens + Pacha, or roasted crucifers + greens
Vegetables
Cucumber, broccoli, avocado
Toppings
Mango, pickled red onion, mint, scallion, cashews + hemp
Sauce
Spicy yuzu–ginger vinaigrette
Cook the salmon

Pat dry. Rub with olive oil, salt and pepper. Roast at 425°F for about 8–12 minutes, depending on thickness, until the center reaches 145°F. Rest 2 minutes, then flake over the bowl.

Cook fresh

Lemon-dill white fish

Base
Greens + Pacha, or roasted cauliflower + greens
Vegetables
Cucumber, tomato, broccoli
Toppings
Pickled red onion, dill, parsley, walnuts
Sauce
Champagne–dill vinaigrette
Cook the haddock or bass

Set on an oiled sheet pan. Season with olive oil, lemon, salt and pepper. Roast at 425°F for about 8–12 minutes, until opaque and 145°F in the thickest part.

Mix fresh

Mediterranean tuna

Base
Romaine or mixed greens + Pacha
Vegetables
Tomato, cucumber, celery, black olives
Toppings
Pickled onion, feta, parsley, basil, walnuts
Sauce
Mediterranean vinaigrette
Make the tuna

Drain tuna and mix with chopped celery, cornichons, 1–2 spoonfuls cottage cheese or yogurt, lemon, Dijon, dill or parsley and black pepper. Scoop onto the bowl at serving.

Toppings, not a mystery

Cauliflower with dates + feta

Base
Roasted cauliflower + fresh greens
Vegetables
Cucumber and tomato
Toppings
Chopped dates, crumbled feta, pickled onion, mint, parsley, walnuts + hemp
Sauce
Champagne–dill vinaigrette
Assemble it

Dress the greens lightly. Add warm or room-temperature cauliflower, then sprinkle 1 chopped date and 2–3 tablespoons feta per bowl. Add crisp tofu if you want a fuller plant protein.

Cook fresh

Apricot-sage chicken

Base
Crucifers + greens; spaghetti squash is an optional swap
Vegetables
Brussels sprouts, mushrooms, tomato
Toppings
Chopped dried apricot, pickled onion, sage, parsley, macadamia
Sauce
Sherry–sage vinaigrette
Cook the chicken

Use thin cutlets. Rub with olive oil, salt, pepper and chopped sage. Pan-cook over medium heat for roughly 5–7 minutes per side, or roast at 425°F, until the center reaches 165°F. Rest, slice and add warm.

Cook fresh

Apricot-sage turkey

Base
Crucifers + greens, or a small scoop of quinoa + greens
Vegetables
Brussels sprouts, mushrooms, tomato
Toppings
Chopped dried apricot, pickled onion, sage, parsley, macadamia
Sauce
Sherry–sage vinaigrette
Cook the home-ground turkey

Heat 1 tablespoon olive oil. Brown 1 pound ground turkey with chopped onion, garlic, salt, pepper and sage, breaking it into small pieces, until no pink remains and it reaches 165°F. Use about 4–5 ounces per bowl.

Cook fresh

Chili-crisp tofu

Base
Crucifers + greens, or a little quinoa + greens
Vegetables
Broccoli, cucumber, carrot
Toppings
Pickled jalapeño, scallion, cashews + sesame
Sauce
Yuzu–ginger plus crunchy chili oil
Cook the tofu

Press or pat very dry and cube. Toss with 1 tablespoon oil, salt and pepper. Roast at 425°F for 22–28 minutes, turning once, or sear until crisp. Add sauce after cooking.

Cook fresh

Spicy yuzu salmon

Base
Greens + Pacha, or a little quinoa + greens
Vegetables
Cucumber, carrot, avocado
Toppings
Pickled cucumber, optional mango, scallion, parsley, cashew + sesame
Sauce
Yuzu–ginger vinaigrette + spicy aioli
Cook the salmon

Pat dry and season with olive oil, salt and pepper. Pan-sear skin-side down or roast at 425°F until it reaches 145°F. Brush with yuzu dressing only after cooking; this is not a raw or “sushi” preparation.

Reheats well

Slow-cooked mushroom chicken

Base
Greens with optional quinoa or wild rice
Vegetables
Mushrooms, tomato, roasted cauliflower
Toppings
Pickled onion, sage, parsley, walnuts
Sauce
Sherry–sage pan juices
Finish the bowl

Reheat the mushroom chicken thoroughly. Keep the greens cold and crisp, then spoon the warm chicken and mushrooms on top immediately before serving.

When they are actually in the pantry

Occasional swaps

Canned smoked salmon

Open fresh. Use with cucumber, tomato, dill, pomegranate, walnuts and black-currant Dijon.

Sardines

Open fresh. Use with greens + Pacha, tomato, cucumber, olives, pickled onion and Mediterranean vinaigrette.

Smoked sprats

Open fresh only when you have them. Use with cucumber, carrot, scallion, sesame and rice-vinegar chili dressing.

Food-safety temperatures: USDA lists 145°F for fish and 165°F for chicken and ground poultry. Use a food thermometer in the thickest part. USDA temperature chart.
